factor_scores.evidence_summary: 48+ audit reports across 11 firms cover the protocol broadly, but the Code4rena 2023 M-10 finding (exchange-rate manipulation via donation) was dismissed without remediation and subsequently exploited in Feb 2025 and March 2026. The dismissed finding represents a scope mismatch in effect — the audited-but-dismissed pattern allowed a live exploit on deployed bytecode. Newest features (Flash Loan, E-Mode) have recent audit coverage but deployed bytecode commit-hash match is unverified.

Most recent audits were the flash loan suite in October 2025: Certik (2025-10-14, audit #153), Quantstamp (October 2025, audit #154), Hashdit (2025-10-16, audit #155). Earlier in the same window: eMode by Certik (2025-09-19) and Quantstamp (2025-09-03), and Solidity 0.8 upgrade by Certik (2025-08-24) and Quantstamp (2025-08-29). Multiple components audited within 365 days of the 2026-04-28 assessment. Pattern of continuous multi-firm auditing (Certik + Quantstamp + Hashdit + Fairyproof) is present. Core vToken base code (legacy) is older but the recurring multi-firm review pattern over current features is satisfied.

Code4rena 2023-05-venus M-10 (exchange-rate manipulation via donation/direct transfer) was explicitly disputed by Venus — assessed as 'no negative side effects' and not remediated. Post-mortem confirms: 'This vector was identified in a prior Code4rena audit but was assessed as having no negative side effects and was not remediated.' The finding was not marked Resolved — it was dismissed. Result: two exploits using this exact mechanism (Feb 2025 ZKSync ~$716K, March 2026 BNB Chain ~$2.15M).

11 distinct audit firms: Certik, PeckShield, OpenZeppelin, Hacken, Fairyproof, Quantstamp, Pessimistic, Cantina, Code4rena, HashEx, Hashdit. 56+ reports in main repo, 18+ in isolated-pools. Largest audit surface in this M3a batch.
Tier-1 firms: OpenZeppelin, Cantina, Code4rena. Tier-2: Certik, PeckShield, Quantstamp, Hacken, Pessimistic. Boutique/emerging: Fairyproof, HashEx, Hashdit. Multiple Tier-1 firms engaged.

Pattern of multi-firm concurrent auditing before VIP deployment. Flash loan: Certik Oct 2025, Hashdit Oct 2025, Quantstamp Dec 2025. Specific deploy tx timestamps per audit component not independently verified via Etherscan; deploy-to-audit gap could exceed 60 days for some components. Conservative yellow due to unverified timestamps.

The available public material does not establish a formally submitted bug-bounty disclosure that Venus ignored. The dismissed Code4rena audit finding is material to audit-remediation factors, but is not evidence of an ignored bounty disclosure.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: No selfdestruct usage found in VToken.sol, VTokenInterfaces.sol, MarketFacet.sol, SetterFacet.sol, Diamond.sol per direct source inspection. Compound v2 lineage does not use selfdestruct in core lending logic. No audit report flags selfdestruct as a finding.

Diamond.sol uses delegatecall in fallback to dispatch to facets, but targets are determined by admin-controlled _selectorToFacetAndPosition mapping (not user-supplied). SetterFacet shows no user-controlled external call targets. No user-controlled delegatecall target found in source inspection.

Timelock.sol uses target.call(callData) without an allowlist — any address can be targeted by queued proposals. However, execution requires full Governor Bravo proposal lifecycle (quorum, voting period, timelock delay), providing economic and temporal friction. This is the standard Compound-style design shared by most major governance systems. Yellow not red due to governance friction layer.

VToken.sol implements nonReentrant on mint(), redeem(), borrow(), repayBorrow(), liquidateBorrow(). Isolated Pools VToken similarly guards all core operations. Standard Compound v2 _notEntered guard pattern confirmed.
Venus Core Pool operates with BEP-20/ERC-20 standard tokens. No ERC-777 callback hooks or ERC-1155/ERC-721 integrations found in the core lending architecture. Standard token transfer interface only.

No published standalone Slither divide-before-multiply output. Multiple audit firms have reviewed the codebase statically 2023-2025 without flagging this as a critical open issue. Code4rena 2023 identified arithmetic issues (incorrect blocksPerYear constant) suggesting complex math paths exist. Low confidence yellow due to absence of dedicated tool run.

Compound v2 architecture uses expScale (1e18) and mantissa conventions throughout. VToken storage uses initialExchangeRateMantissa and 1e18 scaling. No mixed-decimals finding in any of the 56+ audit reports.

No signed/unsigned confusion finding in any available audit reports. Compound v2 lineage uses uint256 throughout core accounting. Newer code uses Solidity 0.8.25 (built-in overflow protection). Legacy 0.5.x uses established patterns.
No ecrecover usage in core lending contracts (VToken.sol, Diamond.sol). GovernorBravo uses EIP-712 for vote-by-signature with standard pattern. No ecrecover-zero-address finding in any audit report.

GovernorBravo implements EIP-712 for vote-by-signature. Standard Compound v2-style Governor Bravo includes chainId in domain separator. No domain separator omission finding in any governance audit (Cantina, Quantstamp).

Venus does not use UUPS proxy pattern for core contracts. Core Pool uses Unitroller (transparent-proxy-style) and Diamond for Comptroller. Isolated Pools uses OZ upgradeable proxy. UUPS pattern not present; factor is not applicable.

Core Pool VToken.sol initialize() is public with admin check inside body (ensureAdmin(msg.sender)) and state guard (accrualBlockNumber==0), but no OZ initializer modifier. Isolated Pools VToken.sol correctly uses initializer modifier + _disableInitializers() in constructor. The Core Pool pattern is weaker than OZ standard but the combined admin+state guards prevent the one-tx unauthorized re-init exploit. Yellow (not red) because the state guard effectively prevents unauthorized re-initialization post-deploy.

Isolated Pools VToken.sol confirmed: constructor calls _disableInitializers(). Core Pool VToken.sol (legacy Compound-derived): no _disableInitializers in the constructor path. Diamond.sol does not call _disableInitializers(). Split in hygiene between Core Pool (legacy pattern) and Isolated Pools (modern OZ pattern).

56+ audit reports from 11 firms for main repo, 18+ for isolated-pools. Multiple firms auditing the same components simultaneously provides cross-validation. The density of audit coverage relative to codebase complexity is exceptional for a lending protocol.

Full DAO+Timelock. Governance flows GovernorBravoDelegator (on-chain vote) to one of three Timelocks (Critical 1h, FastTrack 6h, Normal 2d). AccessControlManager provides granular per-function permissions. No single admin EOA in the governance execution path.

Venus publishes three BNB Chain guardian roles; the pause/resume guardian is a Safe. The public Safe Transaction Service endpoint reports 3 owners required from 6 for 0x1C2C…AA6B. That is a meaningful but relatively low threshold for a protocol with about $1.22B TVL, so the score is yellow.

GovernorBravo admin is 0x1C2CAc6ec528c20800B2fe734820D87b581eAA6B — confirmed GnosisSafeProxy (not an EOA). Normal Timelock admin transferred from deployer (AcceptAdmin event block 17924603, May 2022) to 0xeAEb3137...9886fCfcb. No current EOA holds primary admin role.

Guardian Safe 0x1C2CAc6ec528c20800B2fe734820D87b581eAA6B is a SafeL2 multisig with threshold 3 and 6 owners. That corrects the prior unconfirmed-threshold evidence. At about $1.26B TVL, 3-of-6 remains below the green peer norm for this factor, so the score remains yellow.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Three-tier timelock: Critical VIP = 1 hour (3600s, confirmed from constructor args on BscScan), FastTrack VIP = 6 hours (21600s), Normal VIP = 2 days (172800s). At $1.26B TVL, the 1-hour Critical VIP timelock is materially inadequate. Factor threshold: green >=48h, yellow 24-47h, red <24h. Critical tier (1h) is deep in red territory.

Mint (VAI): governance VIP path, timelocked. Rescue/sweepToken: Isolated Pools VToken sweepToken to owner() (timelock). Upgrade: Diamond Comptroller via VIP/Timelock. setOracle: ACM-gated. Pause: Guardian multisig can pause immediately (no timelock — intentional emergency mechanism). Pause is untimed by design; all other sensitive actions timelocked. Yellow per taxonomy: 4/5 timelocked (pause is the deliberate exception).

Venus documents separate BNB Chain guardian roles for critical risk parameters, pause/resume, and oracles, alongside distinct Normal, Fast-track, and Critical timelocks. The pause guardian is distinct from the governance-timelock upgrade path. No unsupported historical-cancellation claim is retained.

Venus’s AccessControlManager enforces permissions at contract/function granularity, but the reviewed public sources do not enumerate current holders for every upgrade, fee, and oracle role. Functional separation exists; assignee separation is not established, so the score is yellow rather than green.

GovernorBravoDelegate uses xvsVault.getPriorVotes(voter, proposal.startBlock) for voting weight — checkpointed balance at proposal-start block. XVS token implements checkpoints mapping and getPriorVotes. Flash-loan attack on voting not possible: staked vault balance cannot be flash-borrowed and the checkpoint is historical.

Quorum = 600,000 XVS (2% of 30M supply). Voting uses checkpointed staked vault balances — not live token balanceOf. Flash loans cannot reach quorum by construction. Additionally, XVS price makes a 600K notional a large value to flash-borrow even if the voting mechanism allowed it.

Critical VIP total time: 6h voting + 1h timelock = 7 hours. This is below the 24-hour red threshold. Fast-track VIP: 24h + 6h = 30 hours (yellow range). Normal VIP: 24h + 48h = 72h (green). The Critical VIP path — which can execute any VIP classified as critical — provides only 7 hours for the community to detect and respond.

factor_scores.evidence_detail: Governor Bravo accepts proposal-supplied target/value/signature/calldata arrays and dispatches them to a route-specific timelock. Timelock.executeTransaction uses target.call.value(value)(callData) without an allowlist. Venus documents a Critical VIP as six hours of voting plus a one-hour timelock; the Governor’s guardian can cancel before execution and vote weight is checkpointed. The unrestricted call path combined with the seven-hour Critical route meets the v1.7 red calibration’s short-review-window condition. This does not rely on the unrelated 2025 social-engineering incident as a governance-executor near miss.
factor_scores.evidence_summary: Governor proposals supply arbitrary targets and calldata to Timelock.call without an allowlist; a Critical VIP can complete six hours of voting plus a one-hour timelock. The short execution window makes this unrestricted executor path red under v1.7.

The prior claim of a 2021 governance-attack cancellation is removed: the cited Chainalysis article describes a 2025 social-engineering incident and market pause, not a proposal cancellation.

VIP-600 evidence supports that the post-THE-market sweep/sync implementation change was routed through the Venus governance proposal path. Venus documents a ResilientOracle architecture with Chainlink, RedStone, Pyth and Binance feeds, plus dedicated correlated-token adapters for LSTs/LRTs. The BNB deployment is documented with RedStone main, Chainlink pivot and Binance fallback; published BNB-chain configuration also shows that some paused markets, including SXP, have only a Chainlink entry. Provider diversity is therefore market-specific rather than uniform.

ResilientOracle supports MAIN, PIVOT and FALLBACK roles, and Venus publishes role assignments by market. BNB is listed with RedStone main, Chainlink pivot and Binance fallback; SXP is listed as paused with Chainlink only. The role roster is therefore explicit but not uniformly three-source across all markets, and configuration can be changed through Venus governance.

Venus documents Chainlink, RedStone, Pyth and Binance as ResilientOracle price-feed providers, with dedicated correlated-token adapters for LSTs/LRTs. The XVS bridge contract independently establishes a LayerZero OFT dependency for the governance-token bridge. These public sources support the disclosed oracle and bridge dependencies; they do not establish an exhaustive dependency inventory.

ResilientOracle implements cascading three-tier fallback via try-catch pattern. If main oracle fails (zero price, revert, or BoundValidator rejection against pivot), fallback is tried against pivot. If all three tiers fail or diverge, transaction reverts with 'invalid resilient oracle price'  -  no last-known-price acceptance. Try-catch prevents individual oracle reverts from halting execution. OpenZeppelin May 2023 audit found zero critical/high findings.

Individual oracle failure for major assets (BTC, ETH) is absorbed by 3-tier fallback. Full oracle freeze requires all three tiers to fail simultaneously. Demonstrated breakage: (a) LUNA 2022  -  Chainlink paused feed, stale price exploited for $11M bad debt before maxStalePeriod triggered revert; (b) THE 2026  -  multi-source convergence after 37-min sustained manipulation, $3.7M loss. Thin-liquidity collateral oracles remain the primary residual breakage vector.

Current evidence does not satisfy the RD-F-053 trigger of a primary oracle reading a single spot DEX pool with no TWAP or fallback. Venus THE-market evidence describes ResilientOracle using RedStone/Binance-style aggregation and BoundValidator behavior; the manipulation risk is real but belongs outside this raw spot-DEX factor.
factor_scores.notes: factual-correction #56; accepted after second review where required

factor_scores.evidence_summary: ChainlinkOracle and BinanceOracle do not use TWAP (point-in-time). TwapOracle.sol exists in VenusProtocol/oracle repo for PancakeSwap AMM pools. TWAP window for PancakeSwap-based assets not confirmed from available sources. THE incident used multi-source convergence (functionally TWAP-manipulation-equivalent). No TWAP window < 30 min confirmed as active for major assets; thin-liquidity TWAP exposure unconfirmed.

Chainlink feeds: multi-source aggregation (no single pool depth concern). BinanceOracle: centralized exchange depth (Binance). RedStone: multi-source. THE attack (2026): ~$30M notional collateral created against thin THE order book; liquidation dumped into empty order book. Post-mortem notes 'illiquid collateral demands proportionally stricter parameters.' Systematic liquidity-floor gating for market listings not confirmed as implemented.

ResilientOracle with BoundValidator provides medianization at the protocol adapter layer across 3 diverse providers. Chainlink uses multi-node aggregation (not single pool). BNB has RedStone (main), Chainlink (pivot), Binance (fallback)  -  three independent sources. Major assets do not rely on a single pool or single exchange. For thin-liquidity assets, multi-source can still converge if all venues are manipulated simultaneously (demonstrated in THE attack).

BoundValidator implements a soft circuit-breaker: if price deviation exceeds configured anchor ratio bands, that tier is rejected and next tier is tried. No hard circuit breaker (automatic market pause on >X% deviation). THE incident: BoundValidator rejected Binance feed for ~37 minutes then accepted convergence  -  it did not permanently block the inflated price once both sources agreed. No automatic market-pause trigger for sustained anomalies.

BoundValidator upper/lower anchor ratios are configurable per asset via governance. Example from docs: BNB uses 0.99 - 1.01 (+/-1%). Exact configured bps for all assets not confirmed. THE attack bypassed BoundValidator by sustaining buy pressure until both feeds converged within bands. Post-2026 proposals tighten maxStalePeriod (74 slots) but don't directly recalibrate BoundValidator bands for illiquid assets.

ChainlinkOracle.sol rejects a price when its age exceeds the configured maxStalePeriod. Venus's public Oracle Configuration Update reports that 74 oracle slots required maxStalePeriod reductions and gives CAKE as an example reduced from 24 hours to 120 seconds. The code-level check is present, but the public change record establishes that stale-period configuration had been too wide for some feeds; residual configuration risk remains.

ChainlinkOracle.sol validates only positive prices (answer <= 0 reverts). No upper-bound check for anomalously high prices. No explicit Chainlink aggregator minAnswer/maxAnswer validation. BoundValidator provides indirect upper bound via anchor ratio, but this is cross-validated against another oracle (not the Chainlink aggregator's own min/max). LUNA 2022 incident involved Chainlink pausing at a floor value  -  current maxStalePeriod check mitigates the specific LUNA scenario (stale pause triggers revert) but upper-bound gap remains.

Venus's primary oracle stack (Chainlink/RedStone/Binance) does not use LP token balanceOf for pricing. In-house correlated token oracles (AnkrBNBOracle, SlisBNBOracle, etc.) use staking exchange rates, not raw LP balanceOf. No evidence of donation-manipulable LP-balanceOf pricing in active markets.

Core lending operations (borrow, liquidation, interest accrual) do not rely on external keepers  -  triggered per-interaction (Compound v2 pattern). The LayerZero default DVN acts as a single-point relayer for XVS bridge messages  -  not redundant. Bridge is for governance token only, not lending TVL. No Gelato or Chainlink Automation dependency for core protocol functions confirmed.

DefiLlama's public Venus dashboard displayed $1.047B TVL on 2026-07-24, with $1.043B on BSC. This remains well above the rubric's coverage floor. The dashboard does not expose a dated 30-day TVL change in its publicly retrievable page content, so no trend claim is carried forward; chain concentration is assessed separately.

RD-F-064 is the top-10 wallet-share primitive, not chain concentration. DefiLlama's public dashboard shows that Venus is highly BSC-concentrated, but it does not publish the required top-10 depositor share. No independently verifiable public wallet-concentration aggregation was confirmed for the approved default surface; BSC concentration and the historical THE loss remain assessed in their respective factors.
factor_scores.notes: Chain concentration is not a substitute for the rubric's top-10 wallet-share measurement.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Major assets (BNB, USDT, USDC, BTCB, ETH) have deep BSC DEX liquidity sufficient for orderly liquidation. Long-tail and governance-token collateral is demonstrably insufficient. March 2026 THE exploit: 254 bots executed 8,048 liquidation transactions against the THE/Thena market, yet $2.15M bad debt remained because THE's thin DEX liquidity (DEX price moved from $0.26 to $0.51 through recursive on-chain manipulation) could not absorb the position at scale. This is a live, high-confidence data point for thin-liquidity collateral failure. Isolated pool architecture theoretically ring-fences this risk, but the March 2026 exploit hit the Core Pool (shared liquidity), amplifying the systemic exposure.

DefiLlama's public Venus dashboard displayed $1.047B TVL and $382.72M active loans on 2026-07-24, implying approximately 36.6% protocol-level utilization. That is not a protocol-wide liquidity-crisis signal. The dashboard does not provide a complete market-level utilization series, so this conclusion is limited to the aggregate.

Four documented bad-debt incidents: (1) May 2021 XVS oracle manipulation: ~$100M bad debt (4,100 BTC + 9,600 ETH); (2) May 2022 LUNA/UST collapse (stale Chainlink oracle): ~$11–14M bad debt; (3) February 2025 ZKSync donation attack: ~$717K net bad debt; (4) March 2026 BNB Chain THE donation attack: ~$2.15M bad debt. Total approximately $114M across four distinct incidents. The 2021 and 2022 bad debt was never fully repaid from on-chain reserves. The March 2026 bad debt repayment proposal (~$2.2M from Treasury + Risk Fund) was in community discussion as of March 20, 2026, with execution status unconfirmed as of 2026-04-28. Incidents 3 and 4 are same-root-cause repeats (Compound-fork donation attack), post-Code4rena-2023 disclosure. This is the clearest red factor beyond F070 itself.

Venus enforces liquidation via Comptroller with 50% close factor (standard) and forced liquidation at 100% when flagged. The Core Pool uses shared liquidity; a single large market disruption propagates across the pool (evidenced in 2021). Protocol has since added supply caps, borrow caps, collateral factor reductions, and Risk Stewards for dynamic parameter adjustment. The Risk Fund for Isolated Pools is funded at ~50% of pool income. However, the Core Pool lacks automatic bad debt tracking at the moment (per Risk Fund docs), relying on treasury funding for shortfall resolution. Curator simulation not performed (PH curation required). Historical record shows the protocol has breached 100% collateralization under stress (2021 XVS: >$100M bad debt created). Not confirmed to be currently below 110% under standard parameters; flagged yellow given history.

VAI is Venus's USD-pegged synthetic stablecoin. It is over-collateralized by construction: minting requires at least 200% collateral backing (50% collateral factor applied to Venus-supplied collateral). VAI has a Peg Stability Module (PSM) allowing 1:1 swaps with USDT/USDC at low fees to mechanically anchor the peg. VAI is NOT an algorithmic under-collateralized design (not Terra/LUNA style). However, XVS (governance token) can be used as collateral to mint VAI. XVS is subject to governance-driven emission, concentration, and price manipulation risk (2021 incident: XVS pumped 90% to enable $100M+ bad debt). An XVS price collapse could force VAI-collateral liquidations, creating an indirect soft-algorithmic feedback loop. This is a second-order risk, not a primary algorithmic design flaw. Score: yellow (soft loop risk, not a hard algorithmic design failure).

The prior red evidence proved the donation/supply-cap bypass history but did not prove the literal current RD-F-070 condition: a live empty cToken-style market with zero supply/borrow. VIP-600/VIP-602 introduced the internalCash/syncCash donation-accounting fix for affected vToken markets. Residual vBNB or past exploit concerns are tracked outside this empty-market condition unless a live zero-supply/borrow market is shown.
factor_scores.notes: factual-correction #56; accepted after second review where required

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Isolated Pool market listings require an initialSupply parameter in the AddMarketInput struct, providing a seed deposit before the market goes live. This partially mitigates the zero-supply empty-market condition. However, the March 2026 THE exploit demonstrates the donation attack is effective on active markets with substantial supply (THE market had 12.2M tokens in genuine deposits, representing 84% of the 14.5M supply cap, before the attack). A seed deposit alone does not prevent the donation attack on active markets. For Core Pool markets, no governance-required minimum seed deposit mechanism was identified in public documentation. The seed deposit mitigates the pure zero-supply empty-market scenario but does not cover the active-market donation pathway that was exploited.

New market listings require a Venus Improvement Proposal (VIP) vote via Governor Bravo on BSC — not permissionless. The Risk Stewards framework introduced (deployment parameters proposed February 27, 2026) enables automated supply/borrow cap adjustments within DAO-defined bounds without a full VIP for routine parameter changes, while retaining governance control for new listings and major parameter changes. This represents a moderately high governance threshold appropriate for a $1.26B protocol. The March 2026 THE incident occurred on a VIP-listed market, but this reflects oracle and liquidity risk in market selection rather than a listing governance failure per se.

The March 2026 THE incident directly evidences a failure of borrow cap protection when the underlying collateral market can be manipulated via donation. The 14.5M THE supply cap was bypassed by inflating the exchange rate rather than increasing supply count — circumventing the borrow cap indirectly. The attacker borrowed $14.9M against a market capped at $14.5M tokens. Even had a stricter oracle-based borrow cap been in force, the exchange rate inflation (3.81x) would have allowed proportionally larger borrowing against the manipulated collateral value. Risk Stewards (February 2026) aim to enable dynamic cap adjustment but were not operational at the time of the exploit. Current score: yellow (mechanism present but demonstrated insufficient for thin-liquidity manipulable collateral).

No independently verifiable public source was found that establishes a deployed Venus ERC-4626 implementation with the v1.7.0 virtual-share offset enabled. Public Venus documentation references an ERC-4626 component but does not prove the deployed offset configuration.
factor_scores.notes: Not assessed pending public deployed-contract or verified-source evidence that proves the applicable Venus ERC-4626 offset configuration.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The March 2026 THE incident proves that an active Core Pool market with substantial deposits (12.2M THE before the attack) remained vulnerable to donation-driven exchange-rate inflation; a first-depositor guard would not address that pathway. Isolated Pool listings expose an initialSupply parameter, and the proposed internalCash/syncCash remediation addresses donation accounting for affected vToken markets. RD-F-074's ERC-4626-offset status remains unassessed rather than assumed.
Venus has public mainnet history since November 2020; at the 2026-07-24 refresh date it exceeds the 365-day green threshold.

Four independently documented protocol incidents affect Venus: the 2021 XVS manipulation, 2022 LUNA stale-price event, 2025 ZKSync donation attack, and 2026 BNB Chain THE donation attack. Multiple incidents produced bad debt, satisfying the red threshold.
The independently documented 2021, 2022, 2025, and 2026 Venus incidents exceed the three-incident chronic-exploit threshold.

The February 2025 ZKSync event and March 2026 THE event both used donation-driven vToken exchange-rate manipulation. The 2026 post-mortem and patch proposal identify the same direct-transfer/supply-cap-bypass weakness, supporting a repeated-root-cause red finding.

The most recent verified exploit was the BNB Chain THE donation attack on 2026-03-15. At the 2026-07-24 refresh date, it was 131 days ago: outside the under-90-day red band and within the 90-364-day yellow band.

The post-mortem followed in two days and describes immediate controls. Public remediation proposals specify an internalCash patch and repayment of about $2.203M bad debt, but do not establish compensation for liquidated users or final execution of every measure. The balanced response assessment remains yellow.
Venus published the THE post-mortem on 2026-03-17, two days after the March 15 incident, satisfying the within-30-days green condition.

Venus stated that a complete core-pool re-audit is planned, but reviewed public materials do not establish a reputable post-incident re-audit or incident review as completed by 2026-07-24. Yellow reflects a stated commitment without completed-audit evidence.

The prepared 90-day public-TVl series computes a coefficient of variation of 0.066845 (90 samples; mean about $1.338B), below the 0.15 green threshold. The DeFiLlama dashboard independently exposes the protocol TVL history.

Public incident reporting places Venus's first official response about two hours after the March 15 THE attack and records subsequent market controls. That falls in the 61-240-minute yellow band; the assessment relies only on public reporting.

At least two documented precautionary pause activations occurred in the trailing year: the September 2025 phishing response and the March 2026 THE incident/cross-chain borrow pause. Both have a documented operational reason, meeting the 1-2-pause yellow band.

The patch proposal confirms non-BNB borrowing was paused on 2026-03-20 and would be lifted after patch deployment and validation, but reviewed public sources do not establish the actual unpause date for every affected market. The over-seven-days condition cannot be determined from verified public evidence.

The public governance index and current deployment documentation show upgrades and market changes, but are not a complete historical address-set inventory. No redeployment is established, and no redeployment can be excluded conclusively. Score: gray.

Venus publicly describes a protocol risk reserve for shortfalls, not a named third-party insurance policy. Reviewed public materials do not establish an active Nexus, Unslashed, Sherlock, or equivalent cover nor conclusively inventory all available cover. Score: gray pending independently verifiable coverage evidence.

Public explorer and incident reporting identify Venus governance components and no documented threshold-reduction or timelock-removal incident. The signal remains applicable; continuous configuration-event monitoring is still required.

Venus's public security documentation says it offers a bug bounty program, but does not publish a platform, scope document, or payout cap; the cited Immunefi route is unavailable. This is a material transparency gap for highest-value contracts, but it does not prove that those contracts are out of scope.

Public reporting describes a 2026 external market/oracle attack, but it does not establish whether any Venus team contributor or external integrator used at least $1M of attributable real capital to build insider credibility before a social-engineering attack. The reported external attacker is not sufficient evidence for, or against, this distinct factor.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: 48+ audit reports across 11 firms cover the protocol broadly, but the Code4rena 2023 M-10 finding (exchange-rate manipulation via donation) was dismissed without remediation and subsequently exploited in Feb 2025 and March 2026. The dismissed finding represents a scope mismatch in effect — the audited-but-dismissed pattern allowed a live exploit on deployed bytecode. Newest features (Flash Loan, E-Mode) have recent audit coverage but deployed bytecode commit-hash match is unverified.

Most recent audits were the flash loan suite in October 2025: Certik (2025-10-14, audit #153), Quantstamp (October 2025, audit #154), Hashdit (2025-10-16, audit #155). Earlier in the same window: eMode by Certik (2025-09-19) and Quantstamp (2025-09-03), and Solidity 0.8 upgrade by Certik (2025-08-24) and Quantstamp (2025-08-29). Multiple components audited within 365 days of the 2026-04-28 assessment. Pattern of continuous multi-firm auditing (Certik + Quantstamp + Hashdit + Fairyproof) is present. Core vToken base code (legacy) is older but the recurring multi-firm review pattern over current features is satisfied.

Code4rena 2023-05-venus M-10 (exchange-rate manipulation via donation/direct transfer) was explicitly disputed by Venus — assessed as 'no negative side effects' and not remediated. Post-mortem confirms: 'This vector was identified in a prior Code4rena audit but was assessed as having no negative side effects and was not remediated.' The finding was not marked Resolved — it was dismissed. Result: two exploits using this exact mechanism (Feb 2025 ZKSync ~$716K, March 2026 BNB Chain ~$2.15M).

11 distinct audit firms: Certik, PeckShield, OpenZeppelin, Hacken, Fairyproof, Quantstamp, Pessimistic, Cantina, Code4rena, HashEx, Hashdit. 56+ reports in main repo, 18+ in isolated-pools. Largest audit surface in this M3a batch.
Tier-1 firms: OpenZeppelin, Cantina, Code4rena. Tier-2: Certik, PeckShield, Quantstamp, Hacken, Pessimistic. Boutique/emerging: Fairyproof, HashEx, Hashdit. Multiple Tier-1 firms engaged.

Pattern of multi-firm concurrent auditing before VIP deployment. Flash loan: Certik Oct 2025, Hashdit Oct 2025, Quantstamp Dec 2025. Specific deploy tx timestamps per audit component not independently verified via Etherscan; deploy-to-audit gap could exceed 60 days for some components. Conservative yellow due to unverified timestamps.

Venus's public security documentation says it offers a bug bounty program, but does not publish a program URL, platform, scope, or maximum payout; the referenced Immunefi route is unavailable. That leaves the program's accessibility and incentives only partially evidenced.

The available public material does not establish a formally submitted bug-bounty disclosure that Venus ignored. The dismissed Code4rena audit finding is material to audit-remediation factors, but is not evidence of an ignored bounty disclosure.

No independently verifiable public static-analysis report sufficient to assess exploitable findings was identified for the current deployed Venus contracts.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: No selfdestruct usage found in VToken.sol, VTokenInterfaces.sol, MarketFacet.sol, SetterFacet.sol, Diamond.sol per direct source inspection. Compound v2 lineage does not use selfdestruct in core lending logic. No audit report flags selfdestruct as a finding.

Diamond.sol uses delegatecall in fallback to dispatch to facets, but targets are determined by admin-controlled _selectorToFacetAndPosition mapping (not user-supplied). SetterFacet shows no user-controlled external call targets. No user-controlled delegatecall target found in source inspection.

Timelock.sol uses target.call(callData) without an allowlist — any address can be targeted by queued proposals. However, execution requires full Governor Bravo proposal lifecycle (quorum, voting period, timelock delay), providing economic and temporal friction. This is the standard Compound-style design shared by most major governance systems. Yellow not red due to governance friction layer.

VToken.sol implements nonReentrant on mint(), redeem(), borrow(), repayBorrow(), liquidateBorrow(). Isolated Pools VToken similarly guards all core operations. Standard Compound v2 _notEntered guard pattern confirmed.
Venus Core Pool operates with BEP-20/ERC-20 standard tokens. No ERC-777 callback hooks or ERC-1155/ERC-721 integrations found in the core lending architecture. Standard token transfer interface only.

No published standalone Slither divide-before-multiply output. Multiple audit firms have reviewed the codebase statically 2023-2025 without flagging this as a critical open issue. Code4rena 2023 identified arithmetic issues (incorrect blocksPerYear constant) suggesting complex math paths exist. Low confidence yellow due to absence of dedicated tool run.

Compound v2 architecture uses expScale (1e18) and mantissa conventions throughout. VToken storage uses initialExchangeRateMantissa and 1e18 scaling. No mixed-decimals finding in any of the 56+ audit reports.

No signed/unsigned confusion finding in any available audit reports. Compound v2 lineage uses uint256 throughout core accounting. Newer code uses Solidity 0.8.25 (built-in overflow protection). Legacy 0.5.x uses established patterns.
No ecrecover usage in core lending contracts (VToken.sol, Diamond.sol). GovernorBravo uses EIP-712 for vote-by-signature with standard pattern. No ecrecover-zero-address finding in any audit report.

GovernorBravo implements EIP-712 for vote-by-signature. Standard Compound v2-style Governor Bravo includes chainId in domain separator. No domain separator omission finding in any governance audit (Cantina, Quantstamp).

Venus does not use UUPS proxy pattern for core contracts. Core Pool uses Unitroller (transparent-proxy-style) and Diamond for Comptroller. Isolated Pools uses OZ upgradeable proxy. UUPS pattern not present; factor is not applicable.

Core Pool VToken.sol initialize() is public with admin check inside body (ensureAdmin(msg.sender)) and state guard (accrualBlockNumber==0), but no OZ initializer modifier. Isolated Pools VToken.sol correctly uses initializer modifier + _disableInitializers() in constructor. The Core Pool pattern is weaker than OZ standard but the combined admin+state guards prevent the one-tx unauthorized re-init exploit. Yellow (not red) because the state guard effectively prevents unauthorized re-initialization post-deploy.

Isolated Pools VToken.sol confirmed: constructor calls _disableInitializers(). Core Pool VToken.sol (legacy Compound-derived): no _disableInitializers in the constructor path. Diamond.sol does not call _disableInitializers(). Split in hygiene between Core Pool (legacy pattern) and Isolated Pools (modern OZ pattern).

56+ audit reports from 11 firms for main repo, 18+ for isolated-pools. Multiple firms auditing the same components simultaneously provides cross-validation. The density of audit coverage relative to codebase complexity is exceptional for a lending protocol.

Full DAO+Timelock. Governance flows GovernorBravoDelegator (on-chain vote) to one of three Timelocks (Critical 1h, FastTrack 6h, Normal 2d). AccessControlManager provides granular per-function permissions. No single admin EOA in the governance execution path.

Venus publishes three BNB Chain guardian roles; the pause/resume guardian is a Safe. The public Safe Transaction Service endpoint reports 3 owners required from 6 for 0x1C2C…AA6B. That is a meaningful but relatively low threshold for a protocol with about $1.22B TVL, so the score is yellow.

GovernorBravo admin is 0x1C2CAc6ec528c20800B2fe734820D87b581eAA6B — confirmed GnosisSafeProxy (not an EOA). Normal Timelock admin transferred from deployer (AcceptAdmin event block 17924603, May 2022) to 0xeAEb3137...9886fCfcb. No current EOA holds primary admin role.

Guardian Safe 0x1C2CAc6ec528c20800B2fe734820D87b581eAA6B is a SafeL2 multisig with threshold 3 and 6 owners. That corrects the prior unconfirmed-threshold evidence. At about $1.26B TVL, 3-of-6 remains below the green peer norm for this factor, so the score remains yellow.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The public Safe Transaction Service exposes the guardian’s six owners and 3-of-6 threshold, but no independent custody, ASN, or signer-identity analysis was completed. Co-hosting is therefore not assessed.
The guardian owner set is publicly available from the Safe Transaction Service, but no signer-behavior analysis sufficient to classify a hot-wallet signer was completed. The factor is not assessed.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The Safe owner set is publicly resolvable, but the latest AddedOwner, RemovedOwner, or ChangedThreshold event was not independently established. The factor is not assessed.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Three-tier timelock: Critical VIP = 1 hour (3600s, confirmed from constructor args on BscScan), FastTrack VIP = 6 hours (21600s), Normal VIP = 2 days (172800s). At $1.26B TVL, the 1-hour Critical VIP timelock is materially inadequate. Factor threshold: green >=48h, yellow 24-47h, red <24h. Critical tier (1h) is deep in red territory.

Mint (VAI): governance VIP path, timelocked. Rescue/sweepToken: Isolated Pools VToken sweepToken to owner() (timelock). Upgrade: Diamond Comptroller via VIP/Timelock. setOracle: ACM-gated. Pause: Guardian multisig can pause immediately (no timelock — intentional emergency mechanism). Pause is untimed by design; all other sensitive actions timelocked. Yellow per taxonomy: 4/5 timelocked (pause is the deliberate exception).

Venus documents separate BNB Chain guardian roles for critical risk parameters, pause/resume, and oracles, alongside distinct Normal, Fast-track, and Critical timelocks. The pause guardian is distinct from the governance-timelock upgrade path. No unsupported historical-cancellation claim is retained.

Venus’s AccessControlManager enforces permissions at contract/function granularity, but the reviewed public sources do not enumerate current holders for every upgrade, fee, and oracle role. Functional separation exists; assignee separation is not established, so the score is yellow rather than green.

GovernorBravoDelegate uses xvsVault.getPriorVotes(voter, proposal.startBlock) for voting weight — checkpointed balance at proposal-start block. XVS token implements checkpoints mapping and getPriorVotes. Flash-loan attack on voting not possible: staked vault balance cannot be flash-borrowed and the checkpoint is historical.

Quorum = 600,000 XVS (2% of 30M supply). Voting uses checkpointed staked vault balances — not live token balanceOf. Flash loans cannot reach quorum by construction. Additionally, XVS price makes a 600K notional a large value to flash-borrow even if the voting mechanism allowed it.

Critical VIP total time: 6h voting + 1h timelock = 7 hours. This is below the 24-hour red threshold. Fast-track VIP: 24h + 6h = 30 hours (yellow range). Normal VIP: 24h + 48h = 72h (green). The Critical VIP path — which can execute any VIP classified as critical — provides only 7 hours for the community to detect and respond.

factor_scores.evidence_detail: Governor Bravo accepts proposal-supplied target/value/signature/calldata arrays and dispatches them to a route-specific timelock. Timelock.executeTransaction uses target.call.value(value)(callData) without an allowlist. Venus documents a Critical VIP as six hours of voting plus a one-hour timelock; the Governor’s guardian can cancel before execution and vote weight is checkpointed. The unrestricted call path combined with the seven-hour Critical route meets the v1.7 red calibration’s short-review-window condition. This does not rely on the unrelated 2025 social-engineering incident as a governance-executor near miss.
factor_scores.evidence_summary: Governor proposals supply arbitrary targets and calldata to Timelock.call without an allowlist; a Critical VIP can complete six hours of voting plus a one-hour timelock. The short execution window makes this unrestricted executor path red under v1.7.

GovernorBravoDelegate permits the configured guardian to cancel a proposal before execution. Venus’s deployed-contract registry identifies a dedicated BNB Chain pause/resume guardian. The prior claim of a 2021 governance-attack cancellation is removed: the cited Chainalysis article describes a 2025 social-engineering incident and market pause, not a proposal cancellation.

VIP-600 evidence supports that the post-THE-market sweep/sync implementation change was routed through the Venus governance proposal path. The requested green move is not accepted because the full legacy/Core vToken admin and rescue surface is not exhaustively verified as absent or >=24h timelocked. Score remains yellow.
factor_scores.notes: factual-correction #56; accepted after second review where required

factor_scores.evidence_summary: VAI.sol has unlimited mint(address usr, uint256 wad) gated by auth modifier (wards[msg.sender] == 1). No supply cap on VAI. VAI minting authorization requires governance VIP to add new wards (Normal Timelock, 48h delay). XVS has fixed 30M supply, no mint. Yellow: VAI is uncapped but mint authorization is governance-timelocked — not single-EOA accessible.

Current governance is documented as a Governor/Timelock system, but the inspected evidence does not establish whether the deployer EOA remained the effective admin exactly seven days after launch. The historical deploy-time metric is not assessed.
factor_scores.notes: No launch-plus-seven-days ownership/admin event comparison was completed.

GovernorBravo, all three Timelocks have verifiable constructor args on BscScan matching documented governance topology. Delays confirmed: Critical=3600s, FastTrack=21600s, Normal=172800s. No evidence of silent deviation in observable governance contracts.

Current BNB Chain governance contracts are publicly verifiable, but current explorer verification does not establish whether every relevant contract lacked a public ABI at launch. The launch-time verification metric is not assessed.
factor_scores.notes: No historical explorer-verification-at-launch record was established.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: A community governance post reports 745,057 delegated XVS against a documented 600,000-XVS quorum, a material concentration signal. However, no holder-scan Gini calculation or independent attribution of the delegate was completed, so the score is yellow rather than red.

Venus documents a ResilientOracle architecture with Chainlink, RedStone, Pyth and Binance feeds, plus dedicated correlated-token adapters for LSTs/LRTs. The BNB deployment is documented with RedStone main, Chainlink pivot and Binance fallback; published BNB-chain configuration also shows that some paused markets, including SXP, have only a Chainlink entry. Provider diversity is therefore market-specific rather than uniform.

ResilientOracle supports MAIN, PIVOT and FALLBACK roles, and Venus publishes role assignments by market. BNB is listed with RedStone main, Chainlink pivot and Binance fallback; SXP is listed as paused with Chainlink only. The role roster is therefore explicit but not uniformly three-source across all markets, and configuration can be changed through Venus governance.

Venus documents Chainlink, RedStone, Pyth and Binance as ResilientOracle price-feed providers, with dedicated correlated-token adapters for LSTs/LRTs. The XVS bridge contract independently establishes a LayerZero OFT dependency for the governance-token bridge. These public sources support the disclosed oracle and bridge dependencies; they do not establish an exhaustive dependency inventory.

ResilientOracle implements cascading three-tier fallback via try-catch pattern. If main oracle fails (zero price, revert, or BoundValidator rejection against pivot), fallback is tried against pivot. If all three tiers fail or diverge, transaction reverts with 'invalid resilient oracle price'  -  no last-known-price acceptance. Try-catch prevents individual oracle reverts from halting execution. OpenZeppelin May 2023 audit found zero critical/high findings.

Individual oracle failure for major assets (BTC, ETH) is absorbed by 3-tier fallback. Full oracle freeze requires all three tiers to fail simultaneously. Demonstrated breakage: (a) LUNA 2022  -  Chainlink paused feed, stale price exploited for $11M bad debt before maxStalePeriod triggered revert; (b) THE 2026  -  multi-source convergence after 37-min sustained manipulation, $3.7M loss. Thin-liquidity collateral oracles remain the primary residual breakage vector.

Current evidence does not satisfy the RD-F-053 trigger of a primary oracle reading a single spot DEX pool with no TWAP or fallback. Venus THE-market evidence describes ResilientOracle using RedStone/Binance-style aggregation and BoundValidator behavior; the manipulation risk is real but belongs outside this raw spot-DEX factor.
factor_scores.notes: factual-correction #56; accepted after second review where required

factor_scores.evidence_summary: ChainlinkOracle and BinanceOracle do not use TWAP (point-in-time). TwapOracle.sol exists in VenusProtocol/oracle repo for PancakeSwap AMM pools. TWAP window for PancakeSwap-based assets not confirmed from available sources. THE incident used multi-source convergence (functionally TWAP-manipulation-equivalent). No TWAP window < 30 min confirmed as active for major assets; thin-liquidity TWAP exposure unconfirmed.

Chainlink feeds: multi-source aggregation (no single pool depth concern). BinanceOracle: centralized exchange depth (Binance). RedStone: multi-source. THE attack (2026): ~$30M notional collateral created against thin THE order book; liquidation dumped into empty order book. Post-mortem notes 'illiquid collateral demands proportionally stricter parameters.' Systematic liquidity-floor gating for market listings not confirmed as implemented.

ResilientOracle with BoundValidator provides medianization at the protocol adapter layer across 3 diverse providers. Chainlink uses multi-node aggregation (not single pool). BNB has RedStone (main), Chainlink (pivot), Binance (fallback)  -  three independent sources. Major assets do not rely on a single pool or single exchange. For thin-liquidity assets, multi-source can still converge if all venues are manipulated simultaneously (demonstrated in THE attack).

BoundValidator implements a soft circuit-breaker: if price deviation exceeds configured anchor ratio bands, that tier is rejected and next tier is tried. No hard circuit breaker (automatic market pause on >X% deviation). THE incident: BoundValidator rejected Binance feed for ~37 minutes then accepted convergence  -  it did not permanently block the inflated price once both sources agreed. No automatic market-pause trigger for sustained anomalies.

BoundValidator upper/lower anchor ratios are configurable per asset via governance. Example from docs: BNB uses 0.99 - 1.01 (+/-1%). Exact configured bps for all assets not confirmed. THE attack bypassed BoundValidator by sustaining buy pressure until both feeds converged within bands. Post-2026 proposals tighten maxStalePeriod (74 slots) but don't directly recalibrate BoundValidator bands for illiquid assets.

ChainlinkOracle.sol rejects a price when its age exceeds the configured maxStalePeriod. Venus's public Oracle Configuration Update reports that 74 oracle slots required maxStalePeriod reductions and gives CAKE as an example reduced from 24 hours to 120 seconds. The code-level check is present, but the public change record establishes that stale-period configuration had been too wide for some feeds; residual configuration risk remains.

ChainlinkOracle.sol validates only positive prices (answer <= 0 reverts). No upper-bound check for anomalously high prices. No explicit Chainlink aggregator minAnswer/maxAnswer validation. BoundValidator provides indirect upper bound via anchor ratio, but this is cross-validated against another oracle (not the Chainlink aggregator's own min/max). LUNA 2022 incident involved Chainlink pausing at a floor value  -  current maxStalePeriod check mitigates the specific LUNA scenario (stale pause triggers revert) but upper-bound gap remains.

Venus's primary oracle stack (Chainlink/RedStone/Binance) does not use LP token balanceOf for pricing. In-house correlated token oracles (AnkrBNBOracle, SlisBNBOracle, etc.) use staking exchange rates, not raw LP balanceOf. No evidence of donation-manipulable LP-balanceOf pricing in active markets.

Core lending operations (borrow, liquidation, interest accrual) do not rely on external keepers  -  triggered per-interaction (Compound v2 pattern). The LayerZero default DVN acts as a single-point relayer for XVS bridge messages  -  not redundant. Bridge is for governance token only, not lending TVL. No Gelato or Chainlink Automation dependency for core protocol functions confirmed.

DefiLlama's public Venus dashboard displayed $1.047B TVL on 2026-07-24, with $1.043B on BSC. This remains well above the rubric's coverage floor. The dashboard does not expose a dated 30-day TVL change in its publicly retrievable page content, so no trend claim is carried forward; chain concentration is assessed separately.

RD-F-064 is the top-10 wallet-share primitive, not chain concentration. DefiLlama's public dashboard shows that Venus is highly BSC-concentrated, but it does not publish the required top-10 depositor share. No independently verifiable public wallet-concentration aggregation was confirmed for the approved default surface; BSC concentration and the historical THE loss remain assessed in their respective factors.
factor_scores.notes: Chain concentration is not a substitute for the rubric's top-10 wallet-share measurement.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Major assets (BNB, USDT, USDC, BTCB, ETH) have deep BSC DEX liquidity sufficient for orderly liquidation. Long-tail and governance-token collateral is demonstrably insufficient. March 2026 THE exploit: 254 bots executed 8,048 liquidation transactions against the THE/Thena market, yet $2.15M bad debt remained because THE's thin DEX liquidity (DEX price moved from $0.26 to $0.51 through recursive on-chain manipulation) could not absorb the position at scale. This is a live, high-confidence data point for thin-liquidity collateral failure. Isolated pool architecture theoretically ring-fences this risk, but the March 2026 exploit hit the Core Pool (shared liquidity), amplifying the systemic exposure.

DefiLlama's public Venus dashboard displayed $1.047B TVL and $382.72M active loans on 2026-07-24, implying approximately 36.6% protocol-level utilization. That is not a protocol-wide liquidity-crisis signal. The dashboard does not provide a complete market-level utilization series, so this conclusion is limited to the aggregate.

Four documented bad-debt incidents: (1) May 2021 XVS oracle manipulation: ~$100M bad debt (4,100 BTC + 9,600 ETH); (2) May 2022 LUNA/UST collapse (stale Chainlink oracle): ~$11–14M bad debt; (3) February 2025 ZKSync donation attack: ~$717K net bad debt; (4) March 2026 BNB Chain THE donation attack: ~$2.15M bad debt. Total approximately $114M across four distinct incidents. The 2021 and 2022 bad debt was never fully repaid from on-chain reserves. The March 2026 bad debt repayment proposal (~$2.2M from Treasury + Risk Fund) was in community discussion as of March 20, 2026, with execution status unconfirmed as of 2026-04-28. Incidents 3 and 4 are same-root-cause repeats (Compound-fork donation attack), post-Code4rena-2023 disclosure. This is the clearest red factor beyond F070 itself.

Venus enforces liquidation via Comptroller with 50% close factor (standard) and forced liquidation at 100% when flagged. The Core Pool uses shared liquidity; a single large market disruption propagates across the pool (evidenced in 2021). Protocol has since added supply caps, borrow caps, collateral factor reductions, and Risk Stewards for dynamic parameter adjustment. The Risk Fund for Isolated Pools is funded at ~50% of pool income. However, the Core Pool lacks automatic bad debt tracking at the moment (per Risk Fund docs), relying on treasury funding for shortfall resolution. Curator simulation not performed (PH curation required). Historical record shows the protocol has breached 100% collateralization under stress (2021 XVS: >$100M bad debt created). Not confirmed to be currently below 110% under standard parameters; flagged yellow given history.

VAI is Venus's USD-pegged synthetic stablecoin. It is over-collateralized by construction: minting requires at least 200% collateral backing (50% collateral factor applied to Venus-supplied collateral). VAI has a Peg Stability Module (PSM) allowing 1:1 swaps with USDT/USDC at low fees to mechanically anchor the peg. VAI is NOT an algorithmic under-collateralized design (not Terra/LUNA style). However, XVS (governance token) can be used as collateral to mint VAI. XVS is subject to governance-driven emission, concentration, and price manipulation risk (2021 incident: XVS pumped 90% to enable $100M+ bad debt). An XVS price collapse could force VAI-collateral liquidations, creating an indirect soft-algorithmic feedback loop. This is a second-order risk, not a primary algorithmic design flaw. Score: yellow (soft loop risk, not a hard algorithmic design failure).

The prior red evidence proved the donation/supply-cap bypass history but did not prove the literal current RD-F-070 condition: a live empty cToken-style market with zero supply/borrow. VIP-600/VIP-602 introduced the internalCash/syncCash donation-accounting fix for affected vToken markets. Residual vBNB or past exploit concerns are tracked outside this empty-market condition unless a live zero-supply/borrow market is shown.
factor_scores.notes: factual-correction #56; accepted after second review where required

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Isolated Pool market listings require an initialSupply parameter in the AddMarketInput struct, providing a seed deposit before the market goes live. This partially mitigates the zero-supply empty-market condition. However, the March 2026 THE exploit demonstrates the donation attack is effective on active markets with substantial supply (THE market had 12.2M tokens in genuine deposits, representing 84% of the 14.5M supply cap, before the attack). A seed deposit alone does not prevent the donation attack on active markets. For Core Pool markets, no governance-required minimum seed deposit mechanism was identified in public documentation. The seed deposit mitigates the pure zero-supply empty-market scenario but does not cover the active-market donation pathway that was exploited.

New market listings require a Venus Improvement Proposal (VIP) vote via Governor Bravo on BSC — not permissionless. The Risk Stewards framework introduced (deployment parameters proposed February 27, 2026) enables automated supply/borrow cap adjustments within DAO-defined bounds without a full VIP for routine parameter changes, while retaining governance control for new listings and major parameter changes. This represents a moderately high governance threshold appropriate for a $1.26B protocol. The March 2026 THE incident occurred on a VIP-listed market, but this reflects oracle and liquidity risk in market selection rather than a listing governance failure per se.

The March 2026 THE incident directly evidences a failure of borrow cap protection when the underlying collateral market can be manipulated via donation. The 14.5M THE supply cap was bypassed by inflating the exchange rate rather than increasing supply count — circumventing the borrow cap indirectly. The attacker borrowed $14.9M against a market capped at $14.5M tokens. Even had a stricter oracle-based borrow cap been in force, the exchange rate inflation (3.81x) would have allowed proportionally larger borrowing against the manipulated collateral value. Risk Stewards (February 2026) aim to enable dynamic cap adjustment but were not operational at the time of the exploit. Current score: yellow (mechanism present but demonstrated insufficient for thin-liquidity manipulable collateral).

No independently verifiable public source was found that establishes a deployed Venus ERC-4626 implementation with the v1.7.0 virtual-share offset enabled. Public Venus documentation references an ERC-4626 component but does not prove the deployed offset configuration.
factor_scores.notes: Not assessed pending public deployed-contract or verified-source evidence that proves the applicable Venus ERC-4626 offset configuration.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The March 2026 THE incident proves that an active Core Pool market with substantial deposits (12.2M THE before the attack) remained vulnerable to donation-driven exchange-rate inflation; a first-depositor guard would not address that pathway. Isolated Pool listings expose an initialSupply parameter, and the proposed internalCash/syncCash remediation addresses donation accounting for affected vToken markets. RD-F-074's ERC-4626-offset status remains unassessed rather than assumed.
Venus has public mainnet history since November 2020; at the 2026-07-24 refresh date it exceeds the 365-day green threshold.

Four independently documented protocol incidents affect Venus: the 2021 XVS manipulation, 2022 LUNA stale-price event, 2025 ZKSync donation attack, and 2026 BNB Chain THE donation attack. Multiple incidents produced bad debt, satisfying the red threshold.
The independently documented 2021, 2022, 2025, and 2026 Venus incidents exceed the three-incident chronic-exploit threshold.

The February 2025 ZKSync event and March 2026 THE event both used donation-driven vToken exchange-rate manipulation. The 2026 post-mortem and patch proposal identify the same direct-transfer/supply-cap-bypass weakness, supporting a repeated-root-cause red finding.

The most recent verified exploit was the BNB Chain THE donation attack on 2026-03-15. At the 2026-07-24 refresh date, it was 131 days ago: outside the under-90-day red band and within the 90-364-day yellow band.

The post-mortem followed in two days and describes immediate controls. Public remediation proposals specify an internalCash patch and repayment of about $2.203M bad debt, but do not establish compensation for liquidated users or final execution of every measure. SINGLE DEFAULT DVN (1/1 configuration). Venus XVS bridge uses OFT V2 (BaseOFTV2 from @layerzerolabs/solidity-examples v2). DVN configuration not overridden in contract  -  uses default LayerZero DVN. Venus docs explicitly confirm: 'Bridge relies on a single relayer, the default by LayerZero.' Operator diversity = 0 (single operator = LayerZero Labs). This matches the Kelp DAO 1/1 DVN pattern (Kelp DAO $292M Apr 2026). Mitigants: (a) bridge guards XVS governance token only, not $1.26B lending TVL; (b) BaseXVSProxyOFT rate-limiter (per-tx + daily caps + per-chain mint cap); (c) emergency wallet authorization via VIP in DVN downtime. YELLOW (not RED) because bridge is governance-token-only and rate limiters provide containment. Would be RED if this were the primary lending TVL bridge.

[[critical] CRITICAL per T-14] ResilientOracle stores feed addresses in governance-replaceable mappings. Functions confirmed in source: setOracle(asset, oracle, role), setTokenConfig(TokenConfig), enableOracle(asset, role, bool). Oracle addresses are NOT EVM immutable. Governance (via VIP + applicable Timelock tier) can replace any oracle for any asset. Compound-fork pattern preserves this replaceability  -  oracle is an external call to a mutable mapping. GREEN: no immutable oracle address risk.

TwapOracle.sol exists in VenusProtocol/oracle repo for PancakeSwap AMM pools. PancakeSwap is not fully permissionless-pool-creation in the Uniswap v3 sense. The THE attack (2026) demonstrates that thin-liquidity assets accepted as collateral can be exploited via multi-venue price manipulation  -  functionally equivalent to the permissionless pool oracle attack surface. Isolated pools require governance-approved market listing, providing some gating. Whether any active market uses a fully permissionless-created pool for oracle pricing not confirmed.

Public explorer and incident reporting identify Venus governance components and no documented threshold-reduction or timelock-removal incident. The signal remains applicable; continuous configuration-event monitoring is still required.

Venus's public security documentation says it offers a bug bounty program, but does not publish a platform, scope document, or payout cap; the cited Immunefi route is unavailable. This is a material transparency gap for highest-value contracts, but it does not prove that those contracts are out of scope.

Public reporting describes a 2026 external market/oracle attack, but it does not establish whether any Venus team contributor or external integrator used at least $1M of attributable real capital to build insider credibility before a social-engineering attack. The reported external attacker is not sufficient evidence for, or against, this distinct factor.
factor_scores.notes: No public attribution connecting a Venus contributor or integrator to the required real-capital social-engineering pattern was available in the reviewed evidence.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Venus documents a BNB Chain pause/resume guardian and fine-grained per-market pause controls. Its omnichain executor documentation also describes a daily command limit and pause/resume capability. No bridge asset-outflow cap is established, so the positive mitigation is partial and remains yellow.
